paper_metadata.title: Micro-Shear Bands and Their Enhancement on High Temperature Strength of Mg-Gd-Y-Zr Alloy

evidence.quote: When Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy is cold forged, a large number of nano-micro shear bands are formed inside the grains.

attributes.size: thickness tens to hundreds of nm; length a few micrometers
attributes.location: inside grains, near initial grain boundaries

evidence.quote: considerable micro-shear bands were generated after cold forging with thicknesses ranging from tens of nanometers to hundreds of nanometers and lengths in the range of a few micrometers.

After aging, the precipitates were observed to be almost uniformly distributed in the alloy, as shown in Figure 3b. The SAED pattern has three additional dots as shown in orange, indicating that the precipitates are the β′ phase [19].

attributes.location: inside and outside micro-shear bands and at band boundaries

mechanisms.name: dislocation sliding hindrance by micro-shear band boundaries

evidence.quote: we can conclude that the effective strengthening effect of cold forging on Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy at 200◦C is largely due to the formation of micro-shear boundaries, which act by preventing dislocation sliding.
Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy is a typical age-hardening alloy which is achieved by forming precipitates on the prismatic planes.

mechanisms.name: deformation mode transition from dislocation sliding to grain boundary activity

evidence.quote: the transformation of deformation mode from dislocation sliding to grain boundary activity is mainly due to the change of mechanical properties with temperature.

As micro-shear bands were observed to effectively hinder dislocations sliding, thus higher strength is obtained when deformation is accommodated inside the grains. In the case of deformation accommodated by the grain boundary, the enhancing factors that play a role in the deformation inside the grains no longer contribute to the strength.
